correctness.rationale: The induction calculates each subtree feasibility set conditional on the parent action, proves nonemptiness at parent=0, exclusion of 1 at parent=1 and the necessary flexible case; interval child-count feasibility and separated response counts {0,q} close all cases for q>=2. A four-case hub analysis proves no equilibrium for the explicit triangular unicyclic graph for q>=3. The exact minimal q=3 threshold follows from complete Prüfer tree-plus-nonedge enumeration for orders 3..6, profile-by-profile exhaustive best-response checking, and the verified seven-vertex example. The stand-alone verifier executes these finite certificates; all infinite statements have independent analytic proofs.

originality.rationale: The closest source addresses exactly the pattern Tq but only unrestricted-graph hardness. Prior tree methods decide or find equilibrium conditional on its existence; the present theorem proves unconditional existence on every forest via a structural three-invariant argument and identifies a sharp seven-vertex unicyclic failure for q=3, neither implied by the cited results. Searches of related mathematical records and same-slot claims found no covering implication, subject to unlocated equivalent work.

value.rationale: The motivating picky public-goods response class has an NP-hard existence question on unrestricted graphs. Proving that all forests—not merely paths or those with a positive tree decision—always admit an equilibrium is a qualitative graph-structure boundary with a constructive linear-time witness. Exhibiting and exactly minimizing a one-cycle obstruction demonstrates that a single added cycle can destroy existence, a mathematically motivated threshold rather than an arbitrary finite census.
